explanation.title: Sigmoid Derivative Attenuation
outcomes: Backpropagation over 8+ layers causes 0.25^8 derivative decay
Early layer weights stall almost completely

warning.title: High Vanishing Gradient Risk
warning.message: Sigmoid activation saturates easily at extreme values, restricting derivatives to <= 0.25. Switch to ReLU or GELU to maintain healthier gradient magnitude.

explanation.title: High Learning Rate Instability
outcomes: Large gradient steps overshoot local minima
Risk of loss explosion or NaN values

warning.title: Unstable Training Prediction
warning.message: Learning rate > 0.2 without gradient clipping is prone to divergence. Enable gradient clipping or lower the learning rate.

explanation.title: Batch Normalization Active
outcomes: Zero mean & unit variance enforced per mini-batch
Allows higher learning rates and smoother optimization

explanation.title: Identity Skip Connection Superhighway
outcomes: Additive derivative term (+1) allows gradients to bypass weight layers
Protects early layers from vanishing gradients even at depth > 50
Deeper networks achieve lower training error

explanation.title: Dense Feature Concatenation
outcomes: Direct connections transmit gradients to all preceding layers simultaneously
Feature maps are reused rather than overwritten
High parameter efficiency and multi-channel backprop

comparisons.summary: ResNet maintains strong, non-vanishing gradient flow across deep stacks because identity shortcuts provide direct additive gradient pathways. Standard feedforward VGG stacks decay exponentially as depth increases.
DenseNet connects every layer directly to all subsequent layers via feature concatenation, resulting in multi-channel gradient propagation. ResNet combines features via elementwise addition.

Batch Normalization stabilizes internal layer activation distributions to zero mean and unit variance. Without BatchNorm, internal covariate shift requires tiny learning rates and precise initialization.
Gradient Clipping caps backpropagated derivative norms to a safe threshold, preventing exploding gradients from causing weight oscillations or NaN loss spikes.
